newsitem.title: USA: Menem pledges to fight against corruption.
newsitem.headline: Menem pledges to fight against corruption.

text.p: Argentine President Carlos Menem pledged Wednesday to fight against corruption, saying that those under suspicion will be sent through the court process.
Menem, responding to a question on what he plans to do to combat corruption, said: "We are fighting against corruption. We are sending all those under suspicion to court."

Also asked whether there was any truth to former Economy Minister Domingo Cavallo's charges of corruption, Menem told the America's Society meeting here that although Cavallo's charges will be taken into account "he may be exaggerating from time to time."

Cavallo, the free market reformer dismissed by Menem in July, has named senior Menem ministers and judges in a campaign against graft. He is due in court on December 18 to be tried on charges of slandering a Supreme Court judge.
On the economic front, Menem said Argentina will maintain convertibility and economic stability, and expects economic growth to be no less than five percent in 1997.
The Argentine president also said the country's annualized inflation rate in 1996 will be around minus one percent.
In addition, Menem said there may be news in coming days about labor legislation.
